content.thinking:
I'm tracing the actual cause: the P2 deploy renamed the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics`, but the ServiceMonitor at that commit still selects `port: metrics`, so the mismatch itself is what's visible in the data that actually ran, not something I have to infer from an unobserved reading.

Checking the logs confirms serving continued normally the whole time — error rates and disconnect counts look consistent before and after, so nobody consuming the service would have noticed anything. The real symptom is just that metrics stopped flowing, which I'll phrase concisely with the right citations.

Now I'm building the causal chain: first the observable fact (metrics stopped, service unaffected), then the mechanism (ServiceMonitor's port-name selector matched no port, producing an empty target list per S1 and S2), and I'm about to add the next link tracing this back to the actual port rename in the deploy.

Tracing root cause further — deploy P2 renamed the port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` as of T13, which explains the break. I'm checking whether the earlier deploy P1 should be ruled out, and the metrics data in T5 showing readings up until 10:29 suggests metrics were still being collected successfully while P1 was running, so P1 isn't the culprit — the break lines up with P2's rollout instead.

Also checking T16, which shows no flag changes by anyone other than Argus in the hour before the incident, ruling that out too. The actual mechanism: the rename was applied only to the values file, while the ServiceMonitor in scrape.yaml at the same revision still selected the old `metrics` port name, since D1 only lists values-production.yaml as modified — so nothing caught the mismatch between the two files, which is a contributing gap in the deploy process. That gives the full chain: the port name changed, the ServiceMonitor still searched for the old name, the target list ended up empty, and scraping stopped.

In plain words, this is just: a config change renamed the port the shop exposes metrics on, and the monitoring system kept looking for the old name, so it stopped finding anything to scrape. The risk remains live—since the scrape config still targets a port name nothing provides, metrics and any alerts built on them stay blind to real failures, and I should stick strictly to what the record supports here.

For contributing factors, I'm noting that nothing validates the ServiceMonitor's port name against the actual metrics port, so a single-file rename can fail silently without being caught pre-merge; I'm weighing whether the proposed fix (which adds a test asserting consistency) fully or only partially addresses this gap.

For the second factor, I'm noting an empty scrape target list isn't treated as an operator-facing error, so the problem wasn't flagged until the MetricsAbsent alert fired minutes later — I'm considering whether a target-absent check at deploy time would have surfaced it sooner.

For the third factor, I'm looking at whether on-call was paged at all, since MetricsAbsent wasn't linked to alert routing, meaning the rename that needed manual reverting had no one notified to act on it quickly.

CF-4 about the rename being applied estate-wide looks like a duplicate of CF-1, so I'll skip it. For the code fix, I note F1 targeted main while S1 shows the same issue at the older commit, so the one-line fix needs to carry through a deploy to actually reach production — that's a mitigation step, not a root-cause answer.

Since the older commit's scrape config also selects `port: metrics`, the deployed branch needs the same correction applied before the ServiceMonitor will pick up `http-metrics`. I'm also weighing whether to flag that other estate-wide services might have the same naming drift, though the record only documents it for io-shop's values file — that would be a speculative action item rather than something directly supported by the evidence.

For the lessons section, I'm noting that Argus correctly tied the onset to the deploy after the alert fired, refused to roll back what looked like a deliberate change, and that Code-Fix opened a draft PR shortly after the alert — I want to name what Code-Fix proposed without describing what the fix actually does.

On the went_wrong side, Code-Fix pulled from main rather than the actual running revision, so its draft is written against the wrong branch and needs porting to wherever the deploy happens. I'm also noting nobody paged anyone, and leaving got_lucky mostly empty since the service's uptime during the gap isn't something the logs actually confirm.

For assumptions, I'm checking whether the metrics window overlaps with P1 being in place — since T5 shows series stopping right after 10:29 and P1 happened four hours earlier at 06:30, it seems the window does cover minutes with P1 active, which T5 and T6 together rule out as a cause. I'm also looking at D1, which only touches the production values file.

Now I need to be careful about avoiding plain numbers while still citing identifiers like revision hashes, port labels, and the PR number, since those function as names rather than figures — I'll reference things like "draft PR #358" and the "http-metrics" port name directly, then start laying out the timeline steps referencing the symptom, the P2 deployment, and the revision check without writing out literal time values.

Now I'm drafting the remediation list: deploying a revision with the corrected scrape.yaml as the mitigation, adding a port-name agreement test to pre-merge CI as a prevention measure, and alerting on or gating rollouts when the ServiceMonitor's target list is empty as a detection measure.

I'm also routing MetricsAbsent alerts to on-call paging and checking other services' scrape configs against estate-wide renames. For CF-3, I'm noting that had a person been informed immediately, they could have applied the scrape-config fix Argus couldn't, cutting down the metrics gap, and confirming that logs still show serving continuing as before.

action_items.item: Deploy a revision that carries the corrected deploy/scrape.yaml selecting `http-metrics`. Revision c3c36da's own scrape.yaml still selects `metrics`, and PR #358 was written against main, so the change has to be on the branch that actually deploys.
Run the port-name agreement test proposed in PR #358 as a required pre-merge check on every change under deploy/.
Add an alert or rollout gate that fires when io-shop's ServiceMonitor resolves to no scrape targets.
Route MetricsAbsent on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
Check the scrape configurations of other services that adopted the estate-wide `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` port naming for selectors that still use old port names.

causal_chain.step: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. What was seen instead was that the shop's metrics stopped after the minute at {T5.2} and no samples arrived after that, which raised MetricsAbsent.

The metrics stopped because the scrape found no target. The ServiceMonitor that ran picks the endpoint to scrape by the port name `metrics`, but the running values file names the metrics port `http-metrics`. The ServiceMonitor's own header says that a name matching no port is not an error to the operator but a target list with nothing in it.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f7311966cf37dee314695fe0060867e1ca954 at {P1.1}: the shop's metrics were still being collected with it in place, up to the minute at {T5.2}.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider showed {T16.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T16.3} hour before {T16.4}, and no flags came back when read.

causal_chain.step: No port was named `metrics` because the deploy of revision c3c36da at {P2.1} changed the metrics port's portName from `metrics` to `http-metrics` (and the web and admin ports to `http` and `http-admin`) in deploy/values-production.yaml only. The diff shows no change to deploy/scrape.yaml, so the scrape kept selecting the old name. As of {T13.1}, every replica was running revision c3c36da.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change renamed the port the shop publishes its measurements on, but the monitoring system still looked for the old name, so it stopped finding the shop and stopped collecting its measurements.

contributing_factors.factor: Nothing checks that the port name the ServiceMonitor selects matches `metrics.portName` in the values file; the scrape configuration says so itself. No check of the two files against each other was seen on the change that renamed the port.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A rename that touched only the values file would have been caught before it shipped, and the scrape would have kept finding its target.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: A scrape whose target list is empty is not reported as an error to the operator. The fault was found only when the MetricsAbsent alert saw the series go missing.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The empty target list would have been flagged when the rollout happened, instead of only after the series had been missing for the alert's window.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: MetricsAbsent on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been told as soon as the alert fired and could have made the scrape-configuration change that Argus would not make, shortening the time without metrics.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well: Argus confirmed that every replica was running revision c3c36da {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and it had already read that revision's diff, which shows the metrics port rename.
Argus declined to roll back a change that was made on purpose to test the leading candidate, rather than undoing a deliberate platform-wide rename.
Code-Fix opened draft PR #358 {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, proposing a change to deploy/scrape.yaml and a new test.
went_wrong: Code-Fix read main, which does not contain the running revision c3c36da, so its proposal was written against a revision other than the one that ran. The same change is needed on whichever branch deploys.

input.root_cause: Revision c3c36da renamed the metrics port in deploy/values-production.yaml from `metrics` to `http-metrics` to follow the platform's `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` naming convention. The ServiceMonitor in deploy/scrape.yaml at the same revision still picks its scrape endpoint by the port name `metrics`. Because no port has that name any more, Prometheus's target list for the shop is empty, and that is not reported as an error, so no samples are collected.
input.still_at_risk: The running scrape configuration still looked for a port name that no port in the running deployment had, so the shop's metrics would stay uncollected, and any real trouble in the shop would not show in them or in the alerts built on them.
input.symptom: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped arriving
